newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, in a bid to defuse growing dissent in his party's southern faction, has promised to give it a Cabinet portfolio after three months at the expense of Deputy Industry Minister Somphob Amartayakul. There was no immediate reaction from Somphob, an outsider who joined the Cabinet under the New Aspiration Party's quota and is supposed to be part of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan's economic team. (THE NATION)

- The team of prosecutors responsible for the case against the police who shot and killed six alleged gunmen in Suphan Buri province will thoroughly examine the autopsy results of the six suspects. Relatives of the suspects submitted a petition to the Office of the Attorney General on Tuesday, demanding justice for the dead. t Cabinet reshuffle. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)
Legal loopholes could enable the police to cover up the real cause of death of the six men, says a forensic specialist. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- An alliance of 17 women's groups has announced that it will compete for seats in the Constitution Drafting Assembly, vowing to push for the inclusion of issues men have long ignored or overlooked. The groups will field candidates in 20 provinces with the hope that three women will get through the first round of the election in each of those provinces. (THE NATION)

- Thailand and the Cairns Group of farm exporting nations will pressure members of the World Trade Organisation at a meeting in Singapore next week to begin reviewing the progress of farm liberalisation from next year. Thailand will urge members to state clearly in their declarations what they will do to comply with commitments to the liberalisation of trade in textiles. (THE NATION)

- IBM has officially disclosed plans to build a 14-billion-baht factory in Thailand for the production of disk drives to be used in IBM and other computers worldwide. Construction of the new facility will begin early next year and will incorporate leading-edge manufacturing technologies for final assembly and testing of IBM high-performance disk drives. (BUSINESS DAY)
